items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he’s the one who got me my job many years ago, writing on jazz for the Wall Street Journal

ctx.x: What do you think of jazz journalism in terms of its effect? How valuable is it to people who want to know more about the music and those who do know a lot, but would like to find out what’s happening in it currently, because they can’t be on the scene?

Like everything else, it’s a mixed situation. There was a time when there were very few people writing about it. I mentioned some of the early ones who were very important, like Charles Edward Smith. In terms of what’s happening now, there’s one kind that’s very important, certainly to musicians, because it helps get them gigs, and that’s people who write about “on the scene now,” who cover concerts, reviews, etc., which I don’t do.
